title: Chapter 2952 - 177: Debt Collection and Murder (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 2952: Chapter 177: Debt Collection and Murder (Part 2)

This was his Divinity secretly rejoicing, rejoicing that he was gradually shedding his mortal identity, severing his past memories, erasing his human past, and step by step drawing closer to a true "deity"...

Mo Hua turned his head to look at Big Tiger.

Prompted by "Planting Demon in Taoist Heart," memories with Big Tiger surfaced bit by bit in his mind. Mo Hua remained silent for a long time before finally recalling his own name:

"Mo Hua."

As soon as this name surfaced, Mo Hua felt slightly better, as if his humanity finally had a faint "anchor point."

But at the same time, Mo Hua could sense that this anchor point was gradually loosening.

It seemed that he was becoming somewhat numb to this name as well.

He was already starting to not care who he was, and not care whether he... was even called "Mo Hua" anymore...

Mo Hua pressed his lips tightly together.

Big Tiger seemed to sense something, opened its eyes, and looked at Mo Hua with a melancholy gaze. But it could do nothing, only rub its head against Mo Hua, keeping Mo Hua from being too lonely.

Mo Hua took a deep breath, gently stroked Big Tiger, and sighed:

"I... am fine..."

Big Tiger clearly didn’t believe him, its big eyes blinking rapidly.

Mo Hua shook his head, then stopped letting his mind wander, and continued thinking about Elder You’s matter.

He focused his mind, straining to recall every detail from back then at the Qian Learning State Boundary, looking for clues from his interactions with Elder You.

Yet in his mind, there was still a blank void.

Those people of the past, those events of the past, all seemed like bubbles, existing in illusory unreality.

And in that blankness, whenever he tried to think, his Divine Sense began to throb faintly with pain. That was his Divinity rejecting his human retrospection.

Mo Hua forced himself to be patient, enduring the stabbing pain in his mind, and tried to think bit by bit.

After thinking for a long time, he finally recalled one thing:

Debt!

That Elder You, back at the Qian Learning State Boundary, had "hired" him to do Formation Painting, and owed him one million eight hundred thousand Spirit Stones!

One million eight hundred thousand Spirit Stones!

That was no small sum.

With his human nature already faded, Mo Hua had almost forgotten this matter.

Owing debt is itself owing Cause and Effect; to owe a huge debt and not repay it is to owe a great "Cause and Effect."

In other words, he was now Elder You’s "creditor," while Elder You was a "deadbeat."

This "debt" Cause and Effect was both objective and solid, almost unshakable, and heavy—every bit as heavy as one million eight hundred thousand Spirit Stones.

Even more intriguingly, this was Elder You’s "private debt" to him.

A private debt crossing Great States, unknown to others.

It was questionable whether Elder You himself even remembered that he owed this debt.

After all, debtors are generally not very self-aware.

Which meant this "Cause and Effect Line" was extremely well hidden.

There is a head for every grievance, and a master for every debt.

As long as he followed this predetermined and definite Cause and Effect Line to lock onto Elder You’s whereabouts, he could keep Elder You from escaping Cause and Effect tracking, and might even prevent him from noticing it...

Danger flickered in Mo Hua’s gaze.

"If you don’t pay back what you owe me, you’re going to have to pay interest..."

...

Third Grade, Ghost-Crying Mountain Realm.

A place beyond the control of the Divine Priest’s forces.

An expanse of heavy desert, where gloomy winds howl in rage.

In a certain mountain stronghold, Elder You—who had been lying on the bed resting and nurturing his spirit—suddenly jolted upright.

Expressions shifted across his face, and he muttered under his breath:

"What’s going on? Why am I... suddenly so anxious, my heart pounding like this?"

Elder You’s heart thudded wildly, as if he had committed some enormous sin and was about to face retribution...

"Just what... is going on..."

"Is someone trying to... use Cause and Effect to harm me?"

Elder You hurriedly took out a Sword Talisman and hung it over his heart, then set up twelve Money Jade Mouse statues around himself as protection.

He even put on the Copper Heart Protecting Mirror of Heavenly secret that the Old Ancestor had given him, wearing it on his chest.

Only after doing all this did Elder You feel slightly more at ease, though in his heart he still didn’t understand who was "plotting" against him.

With the Old Ancestor protecting him, who had the ability to scheme against him?

Elder You shook his head, thinking it was just a false alarm, and lay back down to rest with his eyes closed.

During this period, he and that Divine Priest of the Barbaric Wilderness had been taking turns battling openly and covertly, his Heart Spirit overly consumed. He needed to rest properly now and devise some strategies—best would be a once-and-for-all plan to completely rid himself of that damned Divine Priest.

As long as the Divine Priest died, with that greatest enemy gone...

Their Hua family would be able to manipulate the entire Barbaric Wilderness, and then, using the Barbaric Wilderness as a base, control the whole Great Wilderness, to scheme for an even bigger "business"...

"Kill the Divine Priest..."

"Kill the Divine Priest..."

Lying on the bed, Elder You turned this phrase over and over in his heart, imagining that lofty Divine Priest dying in his hands, being skinned and sliced apart. The Fire Qi and resentment in his heart slowly dissipated, and he found a bit of comfort.

These days, Elder You always fell asleep like this.

His enormous business losses had left him grieving like a mourner, with pain carved into his flesh.

If he didn’t indulge in this fantasy, he simply couldn’t close his eyes.

His heart burned with the desire to kill that Divine Priest; within this hatred, Elder You’s mood slowly calmed.

He was then able to properly nourish his spirit.

Time flowed by, bit by bit...

He didn’t know how long had passed; when Elder You opened his eyes again, he suddenly felt the atmosphere in the room had grown a few degrees colder.

As if... it were a room used to store corpses.

At the same time, a coldness nearly devoid of any detectable presence was crawling up his back.

It was clearly extremely frigid and eerie, yet almost imperceptible.

If not for the Sword Talisman at his neck trembling lightly, the Heart Protecting Mirror on his chest glowing, and the Money Rats around him lowly humming, Elder You would not have noticed anything was wrong at all.
